_README: 20 FICTIONAL patient profiles for the trial-matching exercise. No real people.
Written by Claude (Anthropic) at Kerem's request on 13 Nov 2026, BEFORE any trial data was fetched or any matching was run, so the profiles could not be tailored to the trials.

Ages, sexes, symptoms and histories are invented to cover a deliberately wide range of situations a matcher must handle: newly diagnosed and advanced disease, tremor-dominant and gait-dominant, DBS, cognitive impairment, young onset, common comorbidities.
This is a research exercise in text retrieval. It does not determine eligibility and it is not medical advice.

patients.description: 63-year-old man diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease 14 months ago. Tremor-dominant, right hand. Takes levodopa/carbidopa three times daily with good response. No cognitive complaints. Walks independently, still works part time. Interested in trials of new oral medications.

71-year-old woman, Parkinson's for 8 years. Motor fluctuations with wearing-off between levodopa doses and troublesome peak-dose dyskinesia. On levodopa and entacapone. Independent at home but has fallen twice this year. Would consider device or infusion therapies.

45-year-old man with young-onset Parkinson's disease, diagnosed at 42. Strong family history; carries a LRRK2 mutation confirmed by genetic testing. Mild symptoms on rasagiline only, no levodopa yet. Very motivated for disease-modifying and genetic trials.

58-year-old woman diagnosed with Parkinson's disease two months ago. De novo, not yet started on any dopaminergic medication. Mild left-sided bradykinesia and reduced arm swing. Keen to join a trial before starting standard treatment.

77-year-old man, advanced Parkinson's disease for 12 years. Severe gait freezing and postural instability, uses a walking frame, several falls per month. Levodopa response now poor. Mild memory problems but can give informed consent. Carer (wife) attends all appointments.

66-year-old woman with Parkinson's for 6 years and deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus implanted 18 months ago. Good motor control. Now mainly bothered by quiet, slurred speech and mild swallowing difficulty. Interested in speech therapy and rehabilitation studies.

69-year-old man, Parkinson's for 4 years, on a dopamine agonist (pramipexole) and levodopa. Developed an impulse control disorder (compulsive online shopping) attributed to the agonist, now resolving after dose reduction. Also has type 2 diabetes controlled with metformin.

74-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease and significant cognitive decline over the last two years; recent diagnosis of Parkinson's disease dementia. Lives with her daughter. Cannot reliably give informed consent alone. On levodopa and rivastigmine.

52-year-old man, Parkinson's for 2 years, main complaints are severe anxiety, low mood and disturbed sleep with vivid dream enactment (REM sleep behaviour disorder). Motor symptoms mild on rasagiline. Most interested in trials for non-motor symptoms, mood or sleep.

61-year-old woman, Parkinson's for 5 years, moderate symptoms, on levodopa four times daily. Severe constipation and bladder urgency affecting daily life. Enjoys exercise classes; would prefer a non-drug trial such as physiotherapy, dance or exercise.

80-year-old man with longstanding Parkinson's disease, 15 years. Largely wheelchair-bound, marked speech and swallowing problems, recurrent chest infections after choking episodes. On levodopa via dispersible tablets. Family asks about palliative and supportive care research.

49-year-old woman diagnosed with Parkinson's one year ago. Mild tremor and stiffness, not yet on medication. Works full time as a teacher. Has well-controlled asthma. Wants observational or biomarker studies with minimal time commitment, such as blood tests, imaging or wearable sensors.

67-year-old man, Parkinson's for 7 years with marked motor fluctuations, considering advanced therapy. Being assessed for deep brain stimulation but anxious about surgery; would consider focused ultrasound or infusion pump trials instead. On levodopa, opicapone and amantadine.

72-year-old woman, Parkinson's for 3 years, moderate tremor poorly controlled despite levodopa and trihexyphenidyl. Also has atrial fibrillation on apixaban (a blood thinner) and a pacemaker, which has previously excluded her from MRI studies. Looking for drug trials for tremor.

56-year-old man with Parkinson's for 4 years. Main problem is daytime sleepiness and sudden sleep episodes that stopped him driving. On levodopa and a low-dose agonist. Otherwise fit, runs twice a week. Interested in wakefulness or sleep trials and exercise studies.

64-year-old woman, Parkinson's for 10 years, severe off periods with painful dystonia in the early morning. Uses apomorphine rescue injections. Depressed mood treated with sertraline. Would consider continuous infusion trials or new rescue treatments.

59-year-old man with suspected early Parkinson's: 18 months of reduced smell, constipation, REM sleep behaviour disorder and subtle slowing, but diagnosis not yet confirmed by a specialist. No medication. Interested in prodromal or at-risk cohort studies and imaging research.

70-year-old woman, Parkinson's for 6 years, stable on levodopa three times daily. History of breast cancer treated 4 years ago, currently in remission on no cancer treatment. Mild osteoporosis. Wants low-risk trials; previous chemotherapy may exclude her from some studies.

43-year-old woman with young-onset Parkinson's, diagnosed at 41, on rasagiline and occasional levodopa. She and her partner are considering having a child, so she must avoid trials with teratogenic risk or mandatory contraception conflicts. Interested in lifestyle, exercise and digital monitoring studies.

75-year-old man, Parkinson's for 11 years, moderate to severe symptoms, on levodopa five times daily plus safinamide. Chronic kidney disease stage 3 and a previous stroke 5 years ago with full recovery. Vascular history may exclude him from some drug trials; open to observational studies.
